1(a).assumed: Micrometer or calipers on the diameter; repeat in different orientations, average, then halve for radius.

1(b).assumed: Liquid mass = full − empty reading; density = m/V with g to kg and cm³ to m³.

1(c).assumed: Sphere volume 4/3πr³; upthrust = weight of oil displaced = ρVg.

1(d)(i).assumed: Terminal velocity is constant velocity (zero acceleration), found from gradient of the straight part of an s–t graph.

1(d)(ii).assumed: Instantaneous velocity is the gradient of a tangent to the s–t curve.

1(e).assumed: At terminal velocity drag = weight − upthrust; rearrange the given drag formula; derive the unit of η.

2.assumed: Vary M with others controlled; light gate and card give v; plot 1/v² against M; intercept and gradient give R and Q.

3(a).assumed: Equilibrium: zero resultant force in any direction and zero resultant moment about any point.

3(b)(i).assumed: Upward forces equal total downward weights; mass = weight/g.

3(b)(ii).assumed: Sum clockwise moments about A equals anticlockwise moment; solve for the distance.

4(b)(i).assumed: Horizontal velocity is constant, so range = horizontal speed × time.

4(b)(ii).assumed: Final KE = initial KE + GPE lost (or use resultant of components).

4(b)(iii).assumed: Impact angle tan θ = vertical ÷ horizontal velocity components.

5(c).assumed: Incidence 45° exceeds the critical angle, so total internal reflection at each sloping face turns the ray back.

5(d)(i).assumed: At a boundary between two media sin C = n₂/n₁.

5(d)(ii).assumed: Incidence below the new critical angle, so the ray refracts into the lower-index oil, bending away from normal.

6(a).assumed: Electrons act as waves with λ comparable to atomic spacing; graphite crystal orientations make diffraction rings.

7(a)(i).assumed: Parallel heating elements' powers add; I = P/V.

7(a)(ii).assumed: Energy in kW h = kW × hours; multiply by price.

7(c)(i).assumed: Cell and meter symbols; ammeter in series, voltmeter in parallel with the component.

7(c)(iii).assumed: Percentage uncertainties of V and I add for R = V/I.

7(c)(iv).assumed: Smaller current heats wire less; metal resistance rises with temperature, so a cooler wire has lower resistance.

7(c)(v).assumed: Take several readings by varying p.d. and plot V against I; use higher-resolution meters.

8.assumed: Direct and reflected waves superpose; maxima at nλ, minima at (n + ½)λ path difference; Pythagoras gives paths; λ from successive differences.
